headline: Welcome to the live coverage of stage 15 of La Vuelta 26
subtext: The route of stage 15 was modified following the activation of the high temperature protocol after a meeting with representatives of the Commissaires’ Panel, the teams, the riders and La Vuelta management, taking into account all the considerations raised by the different parties and the weather conditions forecast for today. The new route is 110.2 km long from Palma del Rio to Cordoba. The start and the finish are flat, but the middle section is packed with climbing for the attackers to try and upset the field. The neutral start is set at 14:50, the start proper at 15:00 after a 4.1 km parade, and the winners should be crowned at around 17:30.

headline: A new stage town on the map of La Vuelta ahead of a classic finish
subtext: Palma del Rio make its debut as La Vuelta stage town* while Cordoba is a classic venue about to witness a 23rd finish. There are three Andalusian riders in the peloton of La Vuelta 26 (Carlos Rodriguez, Cristian Rodriguez, José Manuel Diaz Gallego) but none of them is from the province of Cordoba. The most emblematic rider from the area is Antonio Gomez del Moral (from Cabra, 75 km south of Cordoba), the winner of three La Vuelta stages, including stage 9 of the 1962 edition with a finish in Cordoba. The future of Andalusian cycling could be defined by Diego Lopez, who was born in Estepona in 2008 and won today the 50th edition of the GP Rüebliland, a staple of the junior calendar. Léo Bisiaux won it in 2023, and Lennard Kämna in 2014. *The full list of new stage towns in this edition: Monaco (stage 1), Manosque (2), Font-Romeu (stage 3), Falset (5), Roquetes (5), Vall d’Alba (7), Puçol (8), Xeraco (8), La Vila Joiosa (9), Alcaraz (10), Elche de la Sierra (10), Vera (12), Almuñécar (13), Palma del Rio (15), Cortegana (16), La Rábida (16), Dos Hermanas (17), El Puerto de Santa María (18), La Calahorra (20), and Collado del Aguacil (20).

headline: The last 2 winners in Cordoba can repeat success today
subtext: In 2021, Magnus Cort dominated a reduced bunch sprint to take the 2nd of his 3 stage wins that year. In 2024, Wout van Aert dominated a reduced bunch sprint to take the 2nd of his 3 stage wins that year. Sepp Kuss was essential to propel him to the victory. Pau Miquel was 3rd. On both occasions, Cordoba witnessed thrilling racing as late attackers were reeled in just before the finish. It was a similar scenario when John Degenkoilb won in Cordoba in La Vuelta 14. The last attacker to win a La Vuelta stage in Cordoba was Peter Sagan in 2011. In his maiden Grand Tour, the young Slovak (21 years old at the time) raced for Liquigas-Cannondale and he participated in a team attack with Vincenzo Nibali, Valerio Agnoli and Eros Capecchi that only Movistar’s Pablo Lastras followed. Sagan eventually took the first of his 18 Grand Tour stage wins. All the aforementioned stages to Cordoba featured the Alto del 14% in the finale. Today, the neighbouring Puerto Artafi is the last categorised summit of the day ahead of the final rush to the line.

headline: Cort: "I expect a breakaway to go to the finish today"
subtext: Magnus Cort (Uno-X Mobility) won in Cordoba in 2021: "I have good memories. It was not a stage I planned to try to win that year, I was in the breakaway the day before so I was taking it easy all day long in the peloton. Suddenly everything came back together for a sprint and I won. I think it can be a reduced bunch sprint but I expect a breakaway to go to the finish today."

headline: Let’s roll
subtext: The peloton make their way to the start proper with a 4.1 km parade.

headline: La Roja
subtext: Enric Mas (Movistar) has been dominant since he claimed La Roja and it was once again impossible for his rivals to distance him yesterday at Sierra de la Pandera. The Spanish climber has a new runner-up: Felix Gall (Decathlon CMA CGM), who trails by 2’06’’, while Primoz Roglic (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) is down to third place with a gap of 2’10’’.

headline: Green jersey
subtext: No change at the top of the points standings: Wout van Aert still leads with 224 points; his Visma-Lease a Bike teammate Matthew Brennan follows with 159 points. Alessandro Romele (XDS Astana) moved a bit closer: 113 points after he was second yesterday’s intermediate sprint.

headline: Polka dot jersey
subtext: Santiago Buitrago (Bahrain Victorious) had to settle for second place in the stage but he significantly increased his lead in the mountains standings: 69 points for the Colombina climber, while Wout Van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike) still has 40. Enric Mas (Movistar) follows with 24 points.

headline: White jersey
subtext: Oscar Onley (Netcompany Ineos) maintained a gap of 30’’ to Jakob Omrzel (Bahrain Victorious) while Léo Bisiaux (Decathlon CMA CGM) now trails by 10’41’’.

headline: Team standings
subtext: XDS Astanahad the best collective performance yesterday and moved up to the second place of the overall team standings, 1h02’02’’ behind Decathlon CMA CGM. Bahrain Victorious are third (+1h12’12’’).

headline: Combativity award
subtext: Kevin Vermaerke (UAE Emirates XRG) will race with a distinctive bib as he was named the most combative rider yesterday.

headline: Stage 15 is ON!
subtext: The route of stage 15 was modified following the activation of the high temperature protocol after a meeting with representatives of the Commissaires’ Panel, the teams, the riders and La Vuelta management, taking into account all the considerations raised by the different parties and the weather conditions forecast for today. The points awarded at the finish don’t change: 30 points for the winner, and the top-15 riders score points, as this is a group 3 stage. The Sprint Zone begins 3 kilometres from the finish line. The time-cut is extended to match the scale of group 5 stages.

headline: A fast pace from the get go
subtext: With a series of attacks and counter-attacks, the riders have already covered 5 kilometres.

headline: The bunch is packed at km 9
subtext: Attacks are flying but Bruno Armirail (Visma-Lease a Bike) covers these moves.

headline: Paleni insists
subtext: Among the most active riders so far today, Enzo Paleni (Groupama-FDJ United) has opened a small gap at km 10. Counter-attackers try to chase him down as they enter the final 100 kilometres of the stage.

headline: 11 leaders: Hayter, Leknessund, Oliveira...
subtext: Frederik Wandahl (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe), Ivo Oliveira (UAE Emirates-XRG), Xabier Mikel Azparren (Pinarello-Q36.5), Enzo Paleni (Groupama-FDJ United), Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step), Andreas Leknessund (Uno-X Mobility), Rudy Porter (Jayco AlUla), Alastair Mackellar (EF Education-EasyPost), Fabian Weiss (Tudor), Reuben Thompson (Lotto-Intermarché), Gijs Leemreize (Picnic-PostNL) are riding 45 seconds ahead of the peloton.

headline: Cofidis at the front of the bunch
subtext: Bryan Coquard (Cofidis), the winner of stage 8 in Xeraco, said this morning he wanted a sprint in Cordoba: “I’m really enjoying it, even though there are tougher moments, like yesterday for example, when it was hard all day long. We want to do well and keep up this momentum. [For a sprint finish in Cordoba, we need] the Cofidis team to control the day, and the Visma team to control it too. It’s a possibility. We’ll see. It’s going to be a very short, very hot and very difficult stage. We’re not at the finish line yet.”

headline: Gap under control?
subtext: The peloton only trail by 1'05'' at km 22. Visma-Lease a Bike work with Cofidis to set the pace in the bunch.

headline: The attackers tackle the first climb of the day
subtext: They face 6.7 km at 4.1% up the Puerto de la Forestal (cat. 3). The peloton trail by 1'05''.

headline: The gap drops down to 50 seconds on the climb
subtext: Steven Kruijswijk (Visma-Lease a Bike) currently sets the pace.

headline: Steinhauser attacks
subtext: Georg Steinhauser (EF Education-EasyPost) sets off from the bunch to try and bridge the 50'' gap to the leaders in the last kilometre of ascent.

headline: Leemreize leads the way to the summit with minimal gaps
subtext: +17'' Steinhauser +33'' Peloton, now paced by Armirail

headline: Results at Puerto de la Forestal (cat. 3, km 34.5)
subtext: 1. Leemreize, 3 pts 2. Porter, 2 pts 3. Leknessund, 1 pt

headline: Steinhauser joins the breakaway
subtext: The peloton are only 25 seconds behind with 70 kilometres to go.

headline: 41.8 km covered in the first hour
subtext: As expected, the pace is relentless today. The last gap: 30 seconds.

headline: Primoz Roglic swaps bikes on a downhill
subtext: The Slovenian won La Vuelta the last two times Cordoba hosted a stage finish, in 2021 and 2024.

headline: Marco Brenner became the 32nd rider to win a Grand Tour stage in 2026
subtext: With Marco Brenner taking his maiden Grand Tour stage win as well as Tudor’s first, 32 riders from 17 teams and representing 15 nations have won Grand Tour stages this year. 8 stage wins - Tadej Pogacar 5 - Jonas Vingegaard 3 - Matthew Brennan, Paul Magnier, Tim Merlier, Jhonatan Narvaez 2 - Richard Carapaz, Remco Evenepoel, Mathieu van der Poel 1 - Wout van Aert, Igor Arrieta, Davide Ballerini, Alberto Bettiol, Marco Brenner, Bryan Coquard, Fredrik Dversnes, Filippo Ganna, Olav Kooij, Sepp Kuss, Andreas Leknessund, Enric Mas, Jonathan Milan, Jakob Omrzel, Mads Pedersen, Jasper Philipsen, Mauro Schmid, Alec Segaert, Thomas Silva, Isaac del Toro, Bastien Tronchon, Michael Valgren, Soren Wærenskjold

headline: 2026 Grand Tour stage wins by teams
subtext: 13 - UAE Emirates XRG 11 - Visma-Lease a Bike 6 - Soudal Quick-Step 3 - Alpecin-Premier Tech, EF Education-EasyPost, Uno-X Mobility, XDS Astana 2 - Bahrain Victorious, Lidl-Trek, Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe 1 - Cofidis, Decathlon CMA CGM, Groupama-FDJ United, Jayco AlUla, Movistar, Netcompany Ineos, Tudor UAE Emirates XRG, Visma-Lease a Bike and Uno-X Mobility have won stages in the three Grand Tours. Lotto Intermarché, NSN and Picnic PostNL are the only WorldTeams who have yet to win a Grand Tour stage in 2026.

headline: 2026 Grand Tour stage wins by nations
subtext: 9 - Slovenia 8 - Belgium 7 - Denmark 5 - Ecuador, France 4 - Italy, Netherlands 3 - Great Britain, Norway 2 - Spain 1 - Germany, Mexico, Switzerland, Uruguay, USA

headline: 50 kilometres to go
subtext: The route is up and down through the Sierra de Hornachuelos. The last gap: 30 seconds.

headline: Novak increases the pace in the bunch
subtext: Kevin Vermaerke is on the Slovenian's wheel. Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike) immediately reacted.

headline: New attacks
subtext: After Novak's acceleration, Michael Gogl (Alpecin-Premier Tech) attacks with 48 km to go. The Austrian national champion is 20 seconds behind the leaders.

headline: Many stragglers
subtext: The pace has significantly increased and pushed riders off the back, including the polka dot jersey wearer Santiago Buitrago (Bahrain Victorious).

headline: Leemreize struggles on a downhill section
subtext: The Dutch attacker is passed by Gogl in pursuit of the breakaway.

headline: Up the Puerto Artafi
subtext: Fabian Weiss (Tudor) and Xabier Mikel Azparren (Pinarello Q36.5) have opened a small gap at the front of the race ahead of the climb up Puerto de Artafi (5.9 km at 5.5%). Reuben Thompson (Lotto Intermarché) rapidly joins them. Andreas Leknessund (Uno-X Mobility) is their closest chaser.

headline: 4 leaders
subtext: Leknessund joined the lead trio. Paleni, Porter, Mackellar and Steinhauser are their closest rivals. The peloton cratch the rest of the attackers (+35'').

headline: Debruyne attacks
subtext: Gogl was the first Alpecin-Premier Tech rider to try and break away. Now it's Debruyne. Leemreize follows him.

headline: Leknessund sets a strong pace into the final 40 kilometres
subtext: Only Azparren can follow the Norwegian, already a stage winner at Aramon Valdelinares (stage 7). Debruyne joins Paleni and Steinhauser in pursuit. The peloton are 20 seconds behind.

headline: Leknessund goes solo
subtext: The Norwegian is 39 kilometres from the finish. Meanwhile, Bryan Coquard (Cofidis) is dropped from the peloton.

headline: Armirail pulls the bunch
subtext: Wout van Aert and Matthew Brennan are on his wheel, and then it's Enric Mas (Movistar) in third position. They are 28 seconds behind the leaders. Debruyne and Weiss are in between.

headline: Leknessund is done with the Puerto de Artafi
subtext: Over the top, Debruyne trails by less than 10 seconds. +20'' Peloton

headline: Results at Puerto de Artafi (cat. 3, km 73.6)
subtext: 1. Leknessund, 3 pts 2. Debruyne, 2 pts 3. Armirail, 1 pt

headline: Debruyne joins Leknessund
subtext: The duo face the final 33 kilometres with a gap of 20 seconds to the bunch.

headline: Debruyne goes first at the intermediate; Van Aert attacks!
subtext: The Belgian icon was fourth at the line, and he kept pushing. He joins the lead duo with 30.5 km to go. Alessandro Romele and Thibau Nys follow.

headline: The situation into the final 30 kilometres
subtext: Van Aert, Nys, Debruyne, Leknessund and Romele lead the way. +12'' Fisher-Black, Johannessen +23'' Peloton

headline: Results of the intermediate sprint (Santa Maria de Trassiera, km 78.9)
subtext: 1. Debruyne, 20 pts / 6'' 2. Leknessund, 17 pts / 4'' 3. Romele, 15 pts / 2'' 4. Van Aert, 13 pts 5. Armirail, 10 pts

headline: 9 chasers
subtext: Ivo Oliveira, Kevin Vermaerke (UAE Emirates XRG), Ed Dunbar (Pinarello Q36.5), Tobias Johannessen (Uno-X Mobility), Alessandro Covi (Jayco AlUla), Stefan Küng (Tudor), Henok Mulubrhan (XDS Astana), Gijs Leemreize (Picnic PostNL) and Urko Berrade (Kern Pharma) are 40 seconds behind the leaders with 25 km to go. The gap to the bunch has increased to 1'25''.

headline: Paleni and Tronchon attack from the bunch
subtext: Groupama-FDJ United want to put Bastien Tronchon in a position to repeat the victory he took in Elche de la Sierra (stage 10).

headline: The leaders are 21 km from the finish
subtext: +45'' Chase group +1'05'' Paleni and Tronchon +1'25'' Peloton

headline: Soudal Quick-Step push the pace in the peloton
subtext: Bryan Coquard (Cofidis) is back here.

headline: The pace drops in the bunch
subtext: With 20 kilometres remaining, the gap increases to 1'55''.

headline: 15 kilometres to go
subtext: The five leaders are on the downhill ahead of the final run-in to Cordoba. The chase group are 45 seconds behind.

headline: Coquard drives the peloton
subtext: The gap is at 1'50'' as the leaders enter the final 10 kilometres.

headline: 8 kilometres to go for the 5 leaders
subtext: +55'' Chase group +1'25'' Paleni and Tronchon +2' Peloton, led by Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe

headline: 5 kilometres to go
subtext: The five leaders are now riding 1'10'' ahead of the chase group. They start looking at each other.

headline: Nys attacks with 3 km to go
subtext: Debruyne is on his wheel. Van Aert reacts to close the gap.

headline: Leknessund counter-attacks...
subtext: Van Aert is vigilant.

headline: Last kilometre
subtext: Van Aert leads the group with Romele on his wheel.

headline: Wout van Aert wins stage 15 of La Vuelta 26!
subtext: His second victory in La Vuelta 26, and his second victory in Cordoba after 2024!

headline: Wout van Aert (Visma I Lease a Bike)
Top 5
subtext: 1. Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike) 2. Alessandro Romele (XDS Astana) 3. Thibau Nys (Lidl-Trek) 4. Ramses Debruyne (Alpecin-Premier Tech) 5. Andreas Leknessund (Uno-X Mobility)
